title: Law 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: Vietnam AI Law took effect on 2026-03-01 establishing the legal framework for AI in Vietnam. The law defines AI systems, prohibited practices, and risk-based classification framework including high-risk AI systems requiring conformity assessment and registration with competent authorities.
limitations: Full text implementation guidance and specific sectoral requirements are still being developed through implementing decrees and circulars. Additional regulations from Ministry of Science and Technology and sectoral ministries may impose additional requirements for healthcare AI specifically.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg specifying high-risk AI systems and requirements
supports_claim: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg took effect on 2026-08-15 specifying the list of high-risk AI systems requiring conformity assessment before deployment. Healthcare AI systems providing diagnosis, treatment support, or patient guidance are explicitly included in Annex to the Decision.
limitations: The Decision provides a high-level list and general requirements. Detailed technical standards, conformity assessment procedures, and accredited bodies for healthcare AI specifically may require additional implementing circulars from relevant ministries.

title: EU AI Act - Regulatory Framework for AI
supports_claim: The EU AI Act establishes a risk-based approach with Annex III high-risk AI systems including AI intended to be used for purposes relating to the health sector. High-risk AI systems must comply with requirements for data governance, technical documentation, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity before market placement. Application dates: high-risk rules apply from August 2, 2027 per AI Omnibus regulation.
limitations: Implementation guidance from EU AI Office and sector-specific requirements from health authorities are still being developed. Conformity assessment procedures and notified bodies for healthcare AI may be finalized closer to the application date.

title: IBM Watson - Wikipedia comprehensive article
supports_claim: IBM Watson for Oncology was launched in 2016 to assist oncologists in identifying suitable cancer treatment options. MD Anderson Cancer Center invested $62 million from 2013-2018 before discontinuing the partnership. Watson Health cost $4 billion to develop but was sold for $1 billion in 2022 to Francisco Partners. IBM lost 10% of stock value attributed to Watson failures. Leadership 'fundamentally did not understand the technology' and pursued applications 'too big and too ambitious' rather than practical implementations.
limitations: Wikipedia is secondary aggregation of public sources. Technical details of Watson's training data, model limitations, and specific recommendation failures are not publicly documented. The case reflects enterprise AI adoption challenges broadly, not all of which apply to consumer healthcare applications.

title: Theranos - Wikipedia comprehensive article
supports_claim: Theranos claimed revolutionary blood testing technology from finger pricks but 2016 studies found 68% of lab measurements showed significant interservice variability. FDA inspections found nanotainers were uncleared medical devices. Regulators found 'immediate jeopardy to patient health and safety' at Newark lab. SEC charged fraud in 2018. Elizabeth Holmes convicted on four counts of wire fraud in January 2022 and sentenced to 11 years 3 months in prison. Sunny Balwani convicted on 12 fraud counts and sentenced to 12 years 11 months.
limitations: Theranos was primarily a physical device company with fraudulent operations, not an AI company per se. The case demonstrates healthcare technology fraud and the dangers of insufficient regulatory oversight, but the specific failure modes differ from AI-based healthcare applications.

title: Racial bias in healthcare AI
supports_claim: Research documents how AI systems in healthcare perpetuate racial bias by learning from historical data reflecting systemic disparities in care delivery. Examples include algorithms recommending different care thresholds based on race that do not reflect biological differences but historical inequities. Studies from Stanford and Harvard show algorithmic bias affects diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and healthcare access for minority populations.
limitations: Most documented bias cases are from US healthcare systems. The specific manifestations and statistical patterns may differ in Vietnam's healthcare context, requiring local validation. The technical mechanisms for bias detection and mitigation are applicable cross-context, but specific thresholds and metrics require local demographic data.

title: FDA guidance on AI/ML-enabled medical devices
supports_claim: FDA published guidance on AI/ML-enabled medical devices addressing bias evaluation, post-market monitoring, and algorithm change protocols. The agency recognizes that AI/ML-based Software as a Medical Device requires special consideration for continuous learning and adaptation. FDA's Predetermined Change Control Plan guidance allows manufacturers to specify types of modifications that may be implemented without premarket review.
limitations: FDA guidance is voluntary framework and regulatory jurisdiction applies to US market. International manufacturers seeking FDA clearance may use this framework as best practice, but it is not a mandatory requirement outside US jurisdiction.
